query: Why do handling times differ by channel and priority?

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: Issue category plausibly drives both which channel/priority a ticket enters through (e.g. security_incident routed as high priority) and how long handling takes, making it a common cause not mentioned in the query.

per_column.name: system_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (platform_wide vs single_user) plausibly affects priority assignment (broad-impact incidents escalated) and directly lengthens handling time, a genuine common cause surfaced from data.

per_column.name: resolution_path
per_column.rationale: The resolution path (code_fix, infrastructure_escalation) is chosen after routing and lies on the causal path from treatment/issue to handling time; it is a mechanism through which time is incurred, so adjusting for it would be a mistake.

per_column.name: issue_complexity
per_column.rationale: Complexity plausibly influences the assigned priority (complex issues prioritised) and independently increases handling time; a genuine unobserved common cause not named in the query.

per_column.name: blocking_factor
per_column.rationale: Blocking factors (awaiting_deploy, awaiting_customer_action) arise during handling and are the immediate mechanism prolonging time; they sit on the causal path rather than being an antecedent common cause.

judge.rationale: The treatments (channel, priority) come from the original table and are named in the query. The system surfaced several new variables from the issue text. Three of them (issue_category, system_scope, issue_complexity) are plausible common causes of both routing/priority and handling time, none named in the query, demonstrating genuine confounder discovery. However two columns (resolution_path, blocking_factor) are mediators/post-treatment mechanisms on the causal path to handling time; treating them as adjustment variables would bias the estimate, which lowers overall quality. So the set partially realises the causal-attribution claim but mixes in post-treatment variables.
